# PRACTICE DIRECTION 34B – FEES FOR EXAMINERS OF THE COURT

pd_part34a

# This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34] Contents of this Practice Direction

## Scope

## 1.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.1] This practice direction sets out –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.1] (1) how to calculate the fees an examiner of the court (‘an examiner’) may charge; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.1] (2) the expenses he may recover.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.1] (CPR Rule 34.8 (3) (b) provides that the court may make an order for evidence to be obtained by the examination of a witness before an examiner of the court).

## 1.2

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.2] The party who obtained the order for the examination must pay the fees and expenses of the examiner.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 1.2] (CPR rule 34.14 permits an examiner to charge a fee for the examination and contains other provisions about his fees and expenses, and rule 34.15 provides who may be appointed as an examiner of the court).

## The examination fee

## 2.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 2.1] An examiner may charge an hourly rate for each hour (or part of an hour) that he is engaged in examining the witness.

## 2.2

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 2.2] The hourly rate is to be calculated by reference to the formula set out in paragraph 3.

## 2.3

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 2.3] The examination fee will be the hourly rate multiplied by the number of hours the examination has taken. For example –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 2.3] Examination fee = hourly rate x number of hours.

## How to calculate the hourly rate – the formula

## 3.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 3.1] Divide the amount of the minimum annual salary of a post within Group 7 of the judicial salary structure as designated by the Review Body on Senior Salaries 1 , by 220 to give ‘x’ ; and then divide ‘x’ by 6 to give the hourly rate .

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 3.1] For example –

## Single fee chargeable on making the appointment for examination

## 4.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.1] An examiner of court is also entitled to charge a single fee of twice the hourly rate (calculated in accordance with paragraph 3 above) as ‘the appointment fee’ when the appointment for the examination is made.

## 4.2

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.2] The examiner is entitled to retain the appointment fee where the witness fails to attend on the date and time arranged.

## 4.3

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.3] Where the examiner fails to attend on the date and time arranged he may not charge a further appointment fee for arranging a subsequent appointment.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 4.3] (The examiner need not send the deposition to the court until his fees are paid – see CPR rule 34.14 (2)).

## Examiner’s expenses

## 5.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 5.1] The examiner of court is also entitled to recover the following expenses –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 5.1] (1) all reasonable travelling expenses;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 5.1] (2) any other expenses reasonably incurred; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 5.1] (3) subject to paragraph 5.2, any reasonable charge for the room where the examination takes place.

## 5.2

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 5.2] No expenses may be recovered under sub-paragraph (3) above if the examination takes place at the examiner’s usual business address.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > 5.2] (If the examiner’s fees and expenses are not paid within a reasonable time he may report the fact to the court, see CPR Rule 34.14 (4) and (5)).

## Footnotes

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 34 > Footnotes] 1. The Report of the Review Body on Senior Salaries is published annually by the Stationery Office. Back to text
